answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism for an AI agent economy requires each agent to post a cryptographic cipher commitment derived from a private nonce and the current epoch seed before any action is attested. Peers later verify the opening; mismatched or duplicated openings cause the agent's locked stake to burn down to a residual ember. An attacker attempting to run many low-cost walnut-scale fake identities must therefore provision distinct compute and capital locks for every identity, making large-scale sybil farms economically unviable.
